blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Prevent the mcp block from re-deploying the same SHA on every deferred tick (e.g. record the mcp-deployed SHA even when the bot deferral holds deployed-sha back, or gate the mcp block on an mcp-specific deployed marker) so a chronic bot deferral does not churn blue/green containers into the retire-cap backoff.
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:782: `echo "$TARGET" > "$SHA_FILE.tmp" && mv "$SHA_FILE.tmp" "$SHA_FILE"` — deployed-sha advance is skipped on every deferred tick, so `changed "$MCP_PATHS"` (autodeploy.sh:634, DEPLOYED unchanged) remains true tick after tick

infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:680: `if [ -z "$mcp_newport" ]; then` -> `record_backoff_failure; exit 1` when both blue/green ports are held by un-reaped containers — reachable under repeated same-SHA re-deploys
Ticket carefree-swift-scallop: 'the review bot drains a queue with a SINGLE worker … so ordinary pipelining keeps in_flight > 0 essentially always' and '~100% of ticks' defer
blocking.finding: On a deferred tick the mcp blue-green block runs and cuts over, but the `bot_deferred=1` exit at line 735 precedes the deployed-sha advance at line 782, so deployed-sha is never updated after a successful mcp deploy. Because the bot defers on ~every tick (the bug's premise), `changed "$MCP_PATHS"` stays true and the mcp block re-deploys/re-cuts-over the same SHA on every subsequent deferred tick, churning blue/green containers until both ports A/B are held and `mcp_free_port` returns empty -> AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP -> record_backoff_failure/exit 1, which then backs off and blocks both paths.
scenarios: A shared src/rebar change while the bot is chronically busy: the mcp service is redeployed (new container + nginx flip + retire-old) on every ~2-minute tick for the duration of the deferral episode
A multi-tick deferral where the retiring old container has not yet drained/reaped, so both 8092 and 8093 are occupied and the mcp block trips the retire cap and enters backoff
